title: IAF Flying Branch (AFCAT)
kicker: Pilot entry into the Indian Air Force

value.body: The Indian Air Force recruits pilots as commissioned officers in its Flying Branch. Graduates enter mainly through AFCAT (Air Force Common Admission Test), held twice a year, followed by an Air Force Selection Board interview, pilot aptitude testing and a medical. A civil Commercial Pilot Licence is not required, but CPL holders get a higher upper age limit. Selected candidates train at the Air Force Academy, Dundigal.

items.label: Age limit
items.note: Up to 26 for holders of a valid DGCA-issued CPL

items.label: Education
items.note: Physics and Maths at Class 12 are also required; minimum marks apply

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Clear the AFCAT written exam, then the AFSB interview, which for the Flying Branch includes a computerised pilot selection test (CPSS), and finally an aircrew medical. NCC Air Wing 'C' certificate holders have a separate special entry. Candidates who have failed CPSS or the pilot aptitude test earlier are generally not eligible again.

value.title: At a glance
items: This is a commissioned officer career, not a civil airline job; terms of service are set by the IAF.
A CPL alone is not enough — the entry also needs a graduate degree.
Civil flying hours do not replace IAF flying training; all pilots train through the Academy.
Medical and eyesight standards for aircrew are strict; check them before preparing.
